title: Grab-and-Move interferes with other Alt keyboard shortcuts even without mouse movement
author: ajkessel
summary: Grab and Move reserves its configured Alt or Win modifier too early, interfering with keyboard-only shortcuts even when no mouse movement occurs.
next_action: Approve a modifier-arbitration design and reproduce both keyboard-only and mouse-modified paths.

confidence.rationale: Switching the configured modifier transfers the failure, strongly implicating hook arbitration; exact event-order behavior still needs tracing.

judgment.rationale: Grab and Move consumes or delays its configured modifier before any mouse drag is established, so unrelated Alt/Win shortcuts require a second keypress. Multiple users reproduced the behavior and changing the Grab and Move modifier transfers the failure to that modifier.
evidence: The reporter's Alt-based AutoHotkey shortcuts recover when Grab and Move is changed to Win.
When Grab and Move uses Win, Win-based shortcuts fail instead while Alt shortcuts recover.
Related reports #47337, #47585, and #47655 describe the same first-keypress loss.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a modifier-arbitration design and reproduce both keyboard-only and mouse-modified paths.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt covers the scoped PowerToys-owned path identified by this lightweight judgment.

proposed_fixes.title: Defer Grab and Move modifier capture until a mouse gesture is committed
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The keyboard hook treats the configured modifier as part of Grab and Move before a qualifying mouse press/movement exists, consuming state needed by unrelated keyboard shortcuts.
plan: Track the modifier without suppressing keyboard-only input until the configured mouse button and drag threshold are reached.
Preserve or replay normal modifier state when the gesture is abandoned or no mouse action occurs.
Keep the existing post-drag Alt-menu suppression limited to completed Grab and Move operations.
verification: Verify Alt- and Win-based AutoHotkey, Keyboard Manager, Terminal, and Command Palette shortcuts work on the first press without mouse input.
Verify Grab and Move still starts reliably and does not activate the window menu after an actual drag.

confidence.rationale: Switching the configured modifier transfers the failure, strongly implicating hook arbitration; exact event-order behavior still needs tracing.

issue_context.summary: Grab and Move reserves its configured Alt or Win modifier too early, interfering with keyboard-only shortcuts even when no mouse movement occurs.
known_information: The issue reproduces on PowerToys 0.99.1 with AutoHotkey 2.
The selected modifier determines which family of shortcuts becomes unreliable.
Users report that pressing another key can disengage Grab and Move and allow the intended shortcut.
The problem is consolidated here after #47271 was closed.
inferences: The low-level hook likely suppresses or changes state for the first modifier chord before a drag threshold is met.
The fix must preserve prevention of unwanted Alt menu activation after a real drag.
issue_context.analysis: The public discussion isolates the conflict to Grab and Move's modifier handling rather than AutoHotkey. A design can defer suppression until a mouse gesture is recognized or replay the modifier path when no drag occurs.
initial_investigation: Reviewed every live comment and related issue references #47271, #47337, #47585, and #47655.
Confirmed #47337 and #47585 remain open while #47271 was closed in favor of continued tracking.

actions.label: Approve modifier-arbitration design
actions.design_summary: Delay Grab and Move modifier suppression until a real mouse gesture begins
actions.note: Approval starts a separate fork-side design workflow; this lightweight judgment contains no full design and performs no GitHub write.

actions.label: Reproduce first-shortcut suppression
actions.note: Maintainer-side verification only; this artifact does not execute the steps or write upstream.

reproduce.version_requirement: Latest stable or Preview PowerToys build
prerequisites: Configure Alt, then Win, as its activation modifier
Configure an AutoHotkey, Keyboard Manager, or Command Palette shortcut using the same modifier
steps: Press the keyboard-only shortcut once without touching the mouse.
Press it a second time and record whether only the second invocation succeeds.
Change Grab and Move to the other modifier and repeat.
reproduce.expected_result: Keyboard-only shortcuts work on the first press, while Grab and Move still activates only for the configured mouse gesture.
